newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn may delay Eurofighter decision further-papers.
newsitem.headline: Bonn may delay Eurofighter decision further-papers.

text.p: The German press reported on Saturday that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet may delay a decision on whether to make a firm order for the Eurofighter 2000 combat aircraft until the autumn.

Germany's partners in the project, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's CASA are pressing for the long-awaited decision to get production of the jet underway.

The government has said the decision will be made by the end of this month. But citing unnamed political sources, the respected Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung daily and the news magazine Der Spiegel said this looked increasingly unlikely.
Officials at Bonn's Defence and Finance ministries were not available for comment.

Both said Finance Minister Theo Waigel wanted to hold off the decision until after half-yearly tax estimates in May and suggested this could mean it will be put off until the autumn. Spiegel's report was released ahead of publication on Monday.

German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, who struck a deal to pay 23 billion marks for the 180 Eurofighters Bonn wants to buy -- pricing each aircraft at 125.4 million marks -- told the newspaper he still expected a decision by the end of March.
Ruehe told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that both Kohl's coalition government and the opposition Social Democrats agreed that Germany needed new fighter jets by the year 2002.

"The financial pledges which the finance minister and the coalition made to me in November must be honoured. I cannot cut all my own expenses to finance the planes single-handed," said Ruehe, whose defence budget was trimmed last year as part of Kohl's efforts to cut public spending.
"I'm waiting for the go-ahead from the finance minister and the coalition," Ruehe told the paper in an interview which will be published in full in the paper's Sunday edition.

With state finances under pressure from record unemployment and efforts to fulfil the economic criteria to qualify for the launch of Europe's single currency in 1999, the timing of a decision is sensitive.
Ruehe has said he expects parliamentary approval for the purchase during the first quarter this year, but the timetable suggested by the newspaper indicates a further hold-up.
Germany's partners in the project, Britain, Italy and Spain, are pressing for Bonn to make a firm order to enable the startup of serial Eurofighter production.
